plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A long-cultivated perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and incurved. It is one of the last major garden flowers to bloom in the Northern Hemisphere, and it tolerates light frosts. It is widely grown in gardens, in pots, and commercially for cut flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to East Asia; cultivated worldwide, especially in Japan, China, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are a symbol of the Japanese Imperial family, and Japan holds an annual Chrysanthemum Festival in autumn. The flowers are also used in teas and as a garden ornamental in China.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like leaves that produces huge clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In spring in the Southern Hemisphere, entire streets turn purple, and fallen petals carpet the ground beneath the trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Grafton, Sydney), and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Pretoria in South Africa is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees. In Australia, jacaranda blooms were traditionally said to signal that university exams were near.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms from autumn into early winter, earlier than the common camellia (Camellia japonica). Its flowers are delicate, often lightly fragrant, and open wide with showy yellow stamens. It is popular as a hedge or espalier plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to December in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Mediterranean-climate regions
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. The seeds of some Camellia species are pressed to produce camellia oil, used in cooking and cosmetics.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, a bowl of stiff pink bracts surrounding a central cone of tiny flowers. It thrives in the nutrient-poor, fire-prone fynbos habitat and attracts sunbirds and beetles.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering from October to December in many areas
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of southwestern and southern South Africa; also cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa. The genus Protea is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape, a nod to the great variety of forms in the family.
